META.subject: Essential Mathematics
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 2.3 • 12 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Label,form ratios,compare complementary relationships,measure and qualify a model.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative surveying/design practices;no engineering certification or unsafe field access.
UNIT.focus: Acute right-triangle sine/cosine/tangent,complementary sine/cosine,elevation/depression and actual safe clinometer project.
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional survey report uses the wrong adjacent side and reports rise above eye level as total pole height.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Labelled3–4–5triangle,similar ratios,degree benchmarks,complement table,paper surveys and actual calibrated indoor readings.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: How do reference angles and honest measurements make a triangle model useful? KICD: Why is trigonometry important?
UNIT.storylineThread: Sides → ratios → degree mode → complements → choose ratio → elevation → depression → build → use → application/source → audit → independent model.
UNIT.content: Sines and Cosines of complementary angles; Application of trigonometric ratios (angle of elevation and depression)
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Self-efficacy: The learner makes observations and establishes the relationships between the sine and cosine ratios.
Learning to learn: The learner learns collaboratively while making a simple clinometer using locally available materials and using it as a learning resource.
UNIT.values: Love: The learner demonstrates a caring attitude to others when using a simple clinometer to measure the angle of elevation and depression of different objects in the immediate environment.
UNIT.pcis: Self-esteem: The learners acquire self-esteem while making a simple clinometer using locally available materials and use it as a learning resource.
UNIT.subject: Essential Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
identify the sides of a right-angled triangle in relation to a particular angle,
determine the sine, cosine and tangent of acute angles in a right-angled triangle,
relate sines and cosines of complementary angles,
apply trigonometric ratios to angles of elevation and depression,
recognise the use of trigonometry in real-life situations.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson12,40minutes:4procedure,16sections1–2,12section3,4section4,4checking/collection. Work independently with TR12only,calculator in degree mode and blank paper. No teaching cards,peers,hints or media. Use supplied fictional data,not an actual survey claim;show labelled diagrams,ratios and units. Round final lengths to2decimalplaces where needed.

sections.title: 1. Side names and ratios
sections.prompt: For TR12FinalA,identify hypotenuse,opposite and adjacent leg relative to X;repeat relative to Z. Determine sine,cosine and tangent of both acute angles. Explain which side names change and why ratios have no length units.

sections.title: 2. Complementary relations and degree mode
sections.prompt: Use the triangle to explain sinX=cosZ and cosX=sinZ. State what complementary means. Calculate sin30°,cos60°andtan45°in degree mode and distinguish the exact geometric relation from rounded calculator evidence.

sections.title: 3. Elevation and depression models
sections.prompt: Draw and solve FinalBfor rise above sight level and total pole height. Draw FinalCwith both parallel horizontals;determine horizontal separation and sightline distance. Label reference/right angles,show ratio equations,and state one assumption in each model.

sections.title: 4. A useful application and actual evidence
sections.prompt: Explain one useful real-life trigonometry application with a condition/measurement limit. Describe the horizontal calibration check and how a plumb reading gives the acute elevation/depression magnitude and direction. Name separate actual observations needed to confirm making and using a clinometer in both directions.

SUMMARY_TABLE.drivingQuestion: How do reference angles and honest measurements make a triangle model useful? KICD: Why is trigonometry important?

lessons.title: Which angle gives a side its name?
lessons.observed: Identify hypotenuse,opposite and adjacent leg relative to each acute angle.
lessons.learned: Hypotenuse is fixed by the right angle;opposite/adjacent depend on the reference angle.
lessons.explained: Label sides using a right-angle and reference-angle check.

lessons.title: Why do similar triangles give the same ratios?
lessons.observed: Determine sine,cosine and tangent and explain scale cancellation.
lessons.learned: Ratios compare corresponding lengths and have no length unit.
lessons.explained: Form fractions for both acute angles and compare a scaled triangle.

lessons.title: What changes when a calculator uses degrees?
lessons.observed: Calculate acute-angle ratios in degree mode and find corresponding lengths.
lessons.learned: Mode and angle units determine what a numerical input means.
lessons.explained: Check a benchmark,select a ratio and retain units.

lessons.title: Why does sine match complementary cosine?
lessons.observed: Relate sine/cosine of complementary acute angles geometrically and numerically.
lessons.learned: The same leg is opposite one acute angle and adjacent to its complement.
lessons.explained: Build a complementary table and justify the exact identity.

lessons.title: Which ratio connects the known and needed lengths?
lessons.observed: Choose sine,cosine or tangent for different right-triangle side pairs.
lessons.learned: The ratio is selected from the given reference angle and side roles.
lessons.explained: Draw,label,form an equation and round only the result.

lessons.title: Where does an elevation angle begin?
lessons.observed: Apply tangent to a fictional elevation model with observer-height correction.
lessons.learned: Rise above sight level differs from total height above the ground datum.
lessons.explained: Draw a horizontal-reference triangle and add the correct height offset.

lessons.title: How does depression relate to elevation?
lessons.observed: Apply ratios to a depression model with parallel horizontal references.
lessons.learned: Depression and matching elevation angles are equal under parallel horizontals.
lessons.explained: Draw two horizontals and calculate horizontal/sightline lengths.

lessons.title: Can we build and calibrate a working clinometer?
lessons.observed: Make an actual simple clinometer and verify its horizontal/known-angle calibration.
lessons.learned: A plumb reading needs a correctly aligned pivot/baseline and direction record.
lessons.explained: Assemble safely,check90degree horizontal and a known acute angle.

lessons.title: What do repeated elevation and depression readings show?
lessons.observed: Use the actual clinometer on safe indoor elevated and depressed targets.
lessons.learned: Calibration,reference geometry and reading variation limit a measurement.
lessons.explained: Sight/read/record both directions and compare repeat spread.
